function.text: C4A encodes a complement immune protein expressed by neurons that tags synapses for microglial pruning during development; greater C4A expression is associated with schizophrenia risk.

genes.name: Glutamate ionotropic receptor NMDA type subunit 2A

function.text: GRIN2A encodes the GluN2A NMDA-receptor subunit; rare protein-disrupting variants confer substantial schizophrenia risk, directly implicating glutamate signalling.

genes.name: Glutamate ionotropic receptor AMPA type subunit 3

function.text: GRIA3 encodes the GluA3 AMPA-receptor subunit that mediates fast excitatory transmission; rare coding variants are enriched in schizophrenia.
SETD1A encodes a chromatin-modifying enzyme; rare loss-of-function variants carry large schizophrenia risk, pointing to neurodevelopmental gene regulation.
Deletion of the 22q11.2 region is among the largest known genetic risk factors for schizophrenia, also affecting cardiac, immune and cognitive development.

effect.text: Ultra-rare protein-truncating variants in AKAP11 confer substantial bipolar disorder risk, with a reported odds ratio of about 7 and a gene-level p-value of 2.83e-9.

function.text: AKAP11 encodes a scaffold that localises PKA signalling to specific substrates; at protein level AKAP-11 interacts with GSK3B, the kinase hypothesised as a key target of lithium.

GSK3B is a constitutively active kinase that suppresses signalling including beta-catenin and is the long-hypothesised cellular target of lithium in bipolar disorder, linked to AKAP11 at the protein level.
CHD8 is a chromatin remodeler regulating neuronal development; ultra-rare disruptive variants are enriched among bipolar disorder cases and it interacts with schizophrenia risk genes.
BDNF supports neuronal survival and synaptic plasticity through TrkB and p75 receptors, and BDNF-pathway genes and synaptic gene sets are enriched in large genome-wide studies of depression.

SLC6A4 encodes the serotonin transporter targeted by SSRIs; a promoter polymorphism affecting expression has been studied extensively as a moderator of stress and antidepressant response, though its effect size is small and debated.

genes.name: Glutamate ionotropic receptor AMPA type subunit 1

function.text: GRIA1 encodes the GluA1 AMPA-receptor subunit mediating fast excitatory transmission and plasticity, the pathway through which rapid-acting antidepressants such as ketamine are thought to act.

DLGAP1 encodes a postsynaptic scaffold at excitatory synapses that assembles glutamate receptor and signalling complexes, a candidate gene for cortico-striatal synapse dysfunction in obsessive-compulsive disorder.
SLC1A1 encodes a presynaptic glutamate reuptake transporter that clears synaptic glutamate, central to cortico-striatal glutamatergic signalling implicated in obsessive-compulsive disorder.
BTBD3 regulates transcriptional programmes and circadian timing and has been implicated as a rare-variant risk gene in obsessive-compulsive disorder alongside immunologically related genes.

PARK2 encodes parkin, an E3 ubiquitin ligase in the PINK1-PARKIN mitophagy pathway. In a large multi-ancestry PTSD genome-wide study it was the named gene associated with PTSD, and it is also a known Parkinson's disease gene involved in dopamine regulation.

SLC5A12 encodes a sodium-dependent transporter expressed in brain. In a study of 18362 people with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder starting stimulants it was the only locus to reach genome-wide significance, and only in children, for discontinuation of treatment rather than for the disorder itself.
